changeSummary: Publishes the complete internally reviewed proof of the former Hypothesis 2.2 as Theorem 2.2 and a new companion article. Establishes the Chow obstruction and prescribed curved actual Green pairs, updates six related papers and the homepage, Plan, Progress, routes and proof maps. General source-image vanishing and the separately stated Strong G-to-height foundations retain their status. Previous editions and permanent anchors are preserved.

project.title: Beilinson–Bloch Heights and the Strong Zero-Curvature Green Conjecture
project.subtitle: Actual Green forms, canonical pairings, and arithmetic finiteness
project.summary: The Chow obstruction and prescribed curved actual Green pairs are proved. The principal-push theorem constructs full Beilinson–Bloch height pairings from Strong Green under stated analytic foundations; general obstruction vanishing remains open.
project.motivation:
Heights measure the arithmetic size of geometric objects. On curves, degree-zero divisors lead to the Néron–Tate pairing on the Jacobian. In higher codimension, the corresponding pairing connects algebraic cycles, local intersection theory and arithmetic finiteness.

Theorem 2.2 now supplies the Chow-invariant actual Bott–Chern obstruction and curved Green pairs for every prescribed rational cycle over the original finite valued field, on the exact support complement and against all compact actual tests. Vanishing of that obstruction on homologically trivial Chow classes would give the zero-curvature forms required by Strong Green.

The principal-push theorem (PH16; Theorem 7.5) proves that Strong G at every finite completion in both complementary codimensions gives a canonical real pairing on the full geometrically homologically trivial rational Chow groups, within its stated analytic foundations. Positivity, nondegeneracy and arithmetic finiteness remain further questions.
project.programme: The local construction of the Chow obstruction and prescribed curved actual Green pairs is established. The construction strand now focuses on homological source-image vanishing, numerical certificates and the additional trace or intersection interfaces required by particular height arguments. The properties strand separates curve-visible abelian contributions from the residual Griffiths quotient. Arithmetic regulators, integral lattices and fields of definition provide distinct approaches to Northcott finiteness. A comparison strand relates determinant metrics, local heights and degeneration in families.
